options.title: Hold and Rebalance Calmly
options.best_for: Investors with 10+ year horizon who can accept further short-term volatility
options.content_md:
### Asset Allocation
Maintain current 75/25 equity/bond split. Rebalance to target if equity drifts below 70%.

### Why this works
Historical data: investors who held through 2008 (-52%), 2020 (-34%), and 2022 (-18%) recovered and reached new highs within 2-4 years.

### Pros
- No transaction costs
- No tax realisation event
- Historically optimal for 10+ year horizons

### Cons
- Portfolio may fall further before recovering

### Agent guidance
With 25 years to retirement, holding is likely the right call. Worst-case 2008 GFC: -28% portfolio drawdown, recovered by 2012.

options.title: Defensive Shift — Reduce Equity Exposure
options.best_for: Investors who need to reduce anxiety and accept lower long-term returns
options.content_md:
### Asset Allocation
| Asset | Allocation | Change |
|---|---|---|
| Equity (VTI) | 50% | -25% |
| Short-term bonds (SHY) | 30% | +5% |
| Cash / HYSA | 20% | +20% |

### Why this works
Reduces equity beta by 33%. Limits further downside.

### Pros
- Lower anxiety, sleep at night
- Limits further downside to ~7% if market falls another 20%

### Cons
- Selling into a decline crystallises losses
- STCG tax if held <12 months
- Historically underperforms buy-and-hold over 10+ years

### Agent guidance
Consider only if anxiety is significantly impairing your daily life, or if your actual horizon is shorter than stated.

options.title: Do Nothing — The Inertia Option
options.best_for: Believers in long-term mean reversion who can stomach volatility
options.content_md:
### Asset Allocation
No change. Continue DCA contributions every month.

### Why this works
$10,000 invested in S&P 500 in January 2008 was worth $45,000 by 2024 (+350%), despite living through -52%.

### Pros
- Zero transaction costs, zero tax events
- DCA at lower prices buys more units per dollar

### Cons
- Could fall further

### Agent guidance
If horizon is 15+ years and you won't panic-sell, this is the evidence-based rational choice.

hidden_disclosures: Selling VTI positions held <12 months triggers short-term capital gains tax (up to 37% in US).
VTI has no exit load, but your broker may charge a transaction fee (verify).
Moving to cash (HYSA): inflation at 3.2% erodes $3,200/yr per $100,000 in real terms.
